title: EU-Latin America and Caribbean Joint Declaration on a Digital Alliance
executive_summary: On July 17, 2023, the EU and several Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) countries established the EU-LAC Digital Alliance, a cooperative framework aimed at enhancing digital collaboration. This informal alliance promotes dialogue on various digital issues, including internet governance, cybersecurity, and digital skills development, while emphasizing human rights and inclusivity. It seeks to close digital divides and foster a sustainable digital economy, particularly focusing on empowering women and youth. The alliance will support projects like the BELLA fibre-optic cable and regional Copernicus data centers, with regular meetings to assess progress and adapt priorities. The initiative aligns with the Global Gateway and aims to create a bi-regional Investment Agenda in the digital sector.
characteristics: The EU-LAC Digital Alliance is an informal, values-based framework for cooperation between the EU and Latin American and Caribbean countries, focusing on digital issues.
It promotes a human-centric digital economy, emphasizing universal human rights, privacy, and inclusion, particularly for women and marginalized groups.
The Alliance aims to enhance digital skills, connectivity, and innovation, fostering a responsible digital economy and local industry.
Regular dialogues will facilitate the exchange of best practices and convergence of digital policies, addressing issues like cybersecurity and data protection.
Key initiatives include extending digital infrastructure, implementing Copernicus strategies, and establishing a Digital Accelerator for joint ventures in innovation.

Political Actors: Community of Latin American and Caribbean States
Research and Innovation Actors: Latin American and Caribbean Space Agency (ALCE)
Economic Actors: Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean

practical_applications: Establishment of the EU-LAC Digital Alliance as a framework for cooperation on digital matters between the EU and Latin American and Caribbean countries.
Ongoing support for the BELLA programme, which includes the extension of the BELLA fibre-optic cable to enhance digital connectivity.
Implementation of a regional Copernicus Strategy, including the establishment of two regional Copernicus data centres in Panama and Chile.

Creation of the EU-LAC Digital Accelerator to foster collaboration between EU and LAC corporations, SMEs, and innovative start-ups, with a goal of facilitating at least 40 joint ventures for bi-regional innovation and digital transformation.
Regular periodic dialogue to exchange information and best practices on digital policy, focusing on areas such as data protection, cybersecurity, and artificial intelligence.
Development of a bi-regional Investment Agenda in the digital domain underpinned by the Global Gateway initiative.
commitments: Facilitate and accelerate at least 40 joint ventures for bi-regional innovation and digital transformation by the establishment of an EU-LAC Digital Accelerator.
Implement a regional Copernicus Strategy including two regional Copernicus data centres in Panama and Chile.
Extend the BELLA fibre-optic cable to interested countries to build secure digital backbone connectivity.
Review progress on the commitments on an annual basis.
